content: Rifampin and pexidartinib both increase inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only to the oral forms of these agents. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Pexidartinib has the potential to cause hepatotoxicity, and its coadministration with other hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifampin increases the toxicity of pitavastatin through mechanisms involving other pathways, such as OATP1B1 inhibition, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels of pomalidomide by inducing CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ponatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks of ponatinib underexposure. Monitor for reduced efficacy. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ponesimod by mechanisms involving CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 induction. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Based on limited data, strong inducers of these enzymes may significantly reduce systemic exposure to ponesimod, though the clinical relevance is unclear. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration cannot be avoided, double the pralsetinib dose starting on day 7 of coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. After discontinuing the inducer for at least 14 days, resume the previous pralsetinib dose. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of prednisolone and prednisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of pretomanid by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity, and coadministration with hepatotoxic agents, including alcohol and herbal supplements, should be avoided. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of primaquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of progesterone (intravaginal gel, micronized, or natural forms) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised as alternatives. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of propofol by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin and pyrazinamide increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to additive hepatotoxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of quazepam, quetiapine, quinidine, and quizartinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ranolazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of repaglinide and repotrectinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by mechanisms involving OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Avoid coadministration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. Rifampin increases the levels of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters, which may increase systemic exposure to its active metabolite. Coadministration is not recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ribociclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of rifabutin, rimegepant, and ripretinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ritlecitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to reduced efficacy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of rolapitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Long-term coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may significantly reduce rolapitant efficacy. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of selpercatinib, selumetinib, silodosin, and simvastatin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of siponimod by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers, especially in patients with specific CYP2C9 genotypes (1/3 or 2/3). Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of sirolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity, reducing conversion to its active metabolite. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of solifenacin and sonidegib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of sorafenib by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of sotagliflozin by inducing UGT1A9-mediated glucuronidation. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of sotorasib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Sotorasib also decreases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of stiripentol by inducing CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, increase the stiripentol dose. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by inhibiting OAT1-mediated active secretion. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of tacrolimus and tamsulosin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tazemetostat and temsirolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Tepotinib increases rifampin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of tezacaftor and theophylline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tivozanib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of tizanidine by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tolterodine and tolvaptan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of tovorafenib by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inducers. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of trazodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of triazolam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Trofinetide increases rifampin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid coadministration with sensitive substrates. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tucatinib by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of the typhoid vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
